title: Josiah's death (2 Kgs 23:29) during Necho's march to Harran (ABC 3, Nabopolassar year 17)
proposed_synchronization: 2 Kgs 23:29 has Necho go up "to the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates"; ABC 3 records Aššur-uballiṭ with a large Egyptian army crossing the Euphrates against Harran in Du'ûzu of Nabopolassar's 17th year (609). Josiah fell during that march, before the crossing.
dating_method: Babylonian regnal year fixed by Ptolemy's Canon and astronomical texts (Parker & Dubberstein, via Livius)
via: Necho's 609 campaign (the chronicle does not name Josiah or Megiddo)
assumptions: Kings and the chronicle describe the same Egyptian expedition; the chronicle records Egypt's help to Assyria in 610 and 609, and the 609 crossing is the one that follows Josiah's three-month successor (2 Kgs 23:31–33).

competing_interpretations.label: Expedition against Assyria in 610 (pre-1923 reading)
competing_interpretations.summary: Lumby (1887), before the chronicle was published, dated the expedition to 610 and took it to be against Assyria.

window.basis: Before the Euphrates crossing in Du'ûzu 609 (ABC 3); 1 March is an operator margin.
